acceptance: A test runs RF1 and RF2 on a small (SF 0.01) database, then shows the next run does not reuse it (recreated or refused per the gate decision), with the reason printed.
A test shows a fresh, unrefreshed database is still reused.
The 18 bundles without per-table rows are listed by id with whether any other recorded evidence shows a fresh database; any that ran on a refreshed database is reported, not silently re-labelled.
context:
Decision gate: Choose how refresh state is recorded: a marker written into the database (or a sidecar) when RF1 or RF2 runs, versus recomputing a content checksum at reuse. Criteria: cost at SF 10 and correctness for interrupted refreshes; record the choice. Then choose recreate versus refuse when a refreshed database is found: recreate only inside the BenchBox output root.

Item guardrails: Never delete or recreate a database outside the configured output root; do not change published bundles or their labels in this item; any corpus finding goes to a new item for the owner.

Verification rubric: Pass = both tests green and the 18-bundle list recorded. Fail = a refreshed database reused without a message.

Base guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight), never the primary clone; one PR per repository; no live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs; heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, servers) only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status; never start deliberate CPU, memory or disk load, and tests inject readings instead; comment policy (make comment-policy-check); changelog.d fragment for user-facing change. Re-verify every cited file and line on current develop before acting; they are hints and drift. Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review is re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Origin: Remaining limit recorded at closeout of stale-shared-output-dir-tpch-q18-mismatch-20261114 (PR #4273).
description:
Problem: PR #4273 made database reuse require exact counts for orders and the small tables and lineitem within 0.5%. A database that completed an RF1+RF2 pair keeps the orders count, so only lineitem's 0.5% band can catch it, which is loose at SF 1 and above; refreshed rows change data, not counts. 18 published TPC-H-family bundles record no per-table rows, so the corpus scan could not check them.

Outcome: a reused database records whether refresh functions ran against it, and reuse refuses or recreates a refreshed database regardless of counts.
